articles.headline: Barcelona's start to season is best in Europe's top 5 leagues for almost 100 years
articles.description: Barcelona have begun the season on fire, scoring 36 goals in their first eight matches. How does that compare to the best starts for all time? (Spoiler: Very well.)
articles.body:
LaLiga champions Barcelona have come flying out of the gate this season, with Hansi Flick's freewheeling side picking up where they left off last term and establishing themselves as perhaps the most in-form team on the planet.

Before their campaign was so rudely interrupted by a three-week international break, Barça won their first eight games of the season in all competitions, scoring 36 goals and conceding just eight. That run encompasses seven straight victories in LaLiga and a 5-1 thrashing of Feyenoord in their opening UEFA Champions League fixture.

Just to cement their absurd goal-scoring prowess, the Catalans have somehow managed to hit five goals or more on five separate occasions during those eight games. That is thanks in no small part to the incredible form of winger Raphinha, who has been excelling as a stand-in center forward after his club's summer pursuit of Atlético Madrid striker Julián Álvarez ended in failure.

- Soccer's wildest warmup kits: The good, the bad and the ugly

- Why this international break is longest ever (and that's a good thing)

- 2026 Ballon d'Or: Full men's, women's shortlists, host city, more

The nimble Brazil forward is already well clear at the top of the LaLiga goal-scoring charts with 12 goals from seven games (14 in eight across all competitions) so far. That prolific streak that culminated in back-to-back hat tricks last week, scored in the space of four days in resounding victories over Racing Santander and Sevilla.

After signing off with a "perfect" hat trick (i.e. left foot, right foot, header) against Sevilla, Raphinha can now claim to have made the best goal-scoring start to a season of any Barça player in history. The club captain narrowly pipped the previous record of 13 goals in eight games that was set by Cesar Rodríguez in 1948-49.

Indeed, Raphinha's early scoring form of 12 goals in the first eight LaLiga games of the season has only been bettered once in the 21st century. That was by Cristiano Ronaldo, who scored a frankly astounding 16 goals in eight games for Real Madrid at the start of the 2014-15 season.

Raphinha -- who has somehow missed out on being nominated for the Ballon d'Or -- isn't the only Barça player putting up ridiculous numbers this season. The rejuvenated Lamine Yamal has scored eight goals in as many games while laying on an additional six assists across all competitions -- becoming the youngest player in LaLiga history on record to reach (and subsequently surpass) the 50-assist mark in the process.

In short, things are going well right now at Camp Nou.

Barcelona's performances over the opening eight games of the season have given them a hefty early goal difference of plus-28. It certainly looks highly impressive on paper, but how does Barça's flying start to the campaign compare with the best starts ever made across the top strata of European football?

articles.headline: Who is Liverpool's new sporting director Julian Ward and what does he need to do?
articles.description: Julian Ward has been appointed as Liverpool's sporting director and he'll need to decide the futures of Virgil van Dijk and Alisson Becker, as well as targeting new faces.
articles.body:
And so yet another new Liverpool era begins. It has been a seismic few years at Anfield -- both on the pitch and off it -- with the drastic overhaul of the playing squad mirrored by a significant changing of the guard behind the scenes.

The latest of those changes comes with the appointment of Julian Ward as sporting director, following the departure of Richard Hughes earlier this month after just two years at the helm. Hughes informed the Liverpool hierarchy of his decision to leave the club earlier this year and has now taken up a new role at Saudi Pro League side Al Hilal.

The search for his successor was led by Mike Gordon, the president of club owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG) -- by whom Ward was already employed as technical director. Even before he assumed that role in 2024, Ward was known to Liverpool supporters, having previously worked as the Reds' sporting director for the duration of the 2022-23 campaign.

However, with the landscape at Liverpool having changed markedly in the intervening years, how much of a challenge is Ward facing the second time around? And, in a period of such extreme transition, why is it imperative that he gets things right?

Who is he?

Ward's association with Liverpool dates back to 2012, when he joined from Manchester City to oversee the club's scouting network in Spain and Portugal. Over the next decade, he went on to assume a number of roles in the Reds' football operations department, including loan pathways and football partnerships manager and assistant sporting director to the vaunted Michael Edwards, who was at Liverpool in many roles behind the scenes from 2011-2022 (including a six-year stint as sporting director) and then was CEO of FSG from 2024-2026.

In 2022, after two years as Edwards' deputy, Ward replaced his superior as sporting director, although he only held the position for one season before departing for personal reasons in the summer of 2023. Alongside Edwards, he returned to the FSG fold in 2024, working as technical director as the organization sought to add a second club to its portfolio.

Those plans were officially shelved earlier this year, leading to Edwards' departure in June and subsequently the exit of Hughes following the conclusion of the summer's transfer window.

Born on Merseyside, Ward studied sports science at Liverpool John Moores University and enjoyed his first big break as part of Portugal boss Carlos Queiroz's technical team in 2008. He joined Manchester City in November 2010, with his work as the club's South American scouting strategist coinciding with their first Premier League title triumph in 2012.

Fluent in Portuguese, Ward's relationships in the country -- and in South America -- are viewed as an important asset.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Arsenal, Liverpool eye winger Kevin Schade
articles.description: Arsenal and Liverpool are upping their interest in Brentford's Kevin Schade, while the rest of Europe chases center backs. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Arsenal and Liverpool have identified Brentford's Kevin Schade as a potential addition to their squads, while the rest of Europe chases new center back options.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- There is increasing interest in Brentford winger Kevin Schade from Arsenal and Liverpool, according to Sky Sports. Brentford have held initial talks with the Germany international about extending his contract to see off that interest, with the aforementioned pair being the most serious about signing the 24-year-old when the summer transfer window drew to a close, although Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur are also admirers. Schade has entered the last two years of his current deal and Brentford are keen to offer him improved terms.

- Inter Milan center back Alessandro Bastoni has re-emerged as a transfer option for Barcelona, while Chelsea, Liverpool and Manchester City also retain an interest in him, according to TEAMtalk. The 27-year-old was the topic of serious interest during the summer, but Inter remained firm on their valuation of close to £70 million for the Italy international. Chelsea would benefit from his ability to play in a back three, while Liverpool and City are looking at him as they prepare to eventually lose Virgil van Dijk and Rúben Dias.

- Liverpool, Chelsea and Manchester City are all keen on a potential deal for versatile Atlético Madrid midfielder Marcos Llorente, whose contract expires in the summer, according to TEAMtalk. Madrid are in talks with the 31-year-old over fresh terms and there is confidence within the Spanish club that an agreement will be reached. The situation has still attracted interest from the Premier League, with the trio of giants assessing whether Llorente could become available.

- Real Madrid are keeping an eye on Stuttgart center back Finn Jeltsch, reports Spanish newspaper AS. Madrid have signed Dean Huijsen and Ibrahima Konaté in the last two summer transfer windows but continue their efforts to strengthen the heart of their defence, and they are now monitoring several players from around the world. Jeltsch, 20, received his first Germany call-up from Jürgen Klopp this international window having joined Stuttgart from Nurnberg in January 2025.

- Liverpool are very satisfied with Ronald Araújo during his loan from Barcelona and could trigger their option to permanently sign the defender for €55 million, reports Spanish outlet Mundo Deportivo. The Uruguay international has played seven matches for the Reds, five of those coming as a starter, but he is already convincing the club and Andoni Iraola. The versatility displayed by the 27-year-old to play both right-back and centre-back has also caught the eye.

articles.headline: Which Premier League players got injured in the international break?
articles.description: All the latest news and updates on Premier League stars injuries during the first international break of the 2026-2027 club season
articles.body:
Premier League teams will be watching and hoping their star players remain healthy throughout the international break.

However, some have already sustained injuries while playing for their countries. Premier League matches resume on Oct. 10.

ESPN will be tracking the latest injuries and updates for your club's players:

Kai Havertz (Arsenal)

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the game between Netherlands and Germany on September 24th with what was described as a muscle injury.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," Jurgen Klopp said on RTL about Havertz and Jamal Musiala. "I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

On September 25 the German Football Association confirmed the attacker would be leaving Klopp's camp and return to Arsenal after suffering what they describe as a 'muscle strain.'

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland)

The powerful Sunderland attacker was also injured in the same game after picking up what looked like a hamstring injury while running for the ball. He immediately went down and signalled to the sideline.

He left the field of his own accord but did have a heavy limp as he walked down the tunnel.

Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said after the game: "Brian is indeed injured."

Brobbey was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the Dutch squad.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa)

The goalkeeper linked up with the Japan squad but according to reports missed the main group training session on September 22nd, according to local reports. Instead he was put on an individual session for a rib injury.

Suzuki was subsequently left out of Japan's matchday squad entirely for Thursday's 3-1 victory over Uruguay.

International breaks this season

1. Sept. 21-Oct. 6 (between Premier League gameweeks 5 and 6)

2. Nov. 9-Nov. 17 (between Premier League gameweeks 10 and 11)

3. March 22-March 30 (between Premier League gameweeks 30 and 31)

articles.headline: Sources: Warriors, Curry reach 2-year extension worth $116 million
articles.description: Warriors star Stephen Curry agreed to a two-year, $116 million contract extension, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Friday, ultimately opting for a pay cut and security over a max contract.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry has agreed to a two-year, $116 million contract extension, tying the franchise legend to the only organization he has ever known through his 20th NBA season, league sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Friday.

The deal includes a player option in the final season (2028-29), according to sources. 

The Warriors presented Curry with several contract choices in recent weeks, including the option to wait, but Curry ultimately decided on a pay cut and security over either a max contract or the uncertainty of stalling for more flexibility and information.

Curry is currently on an expiring $62.6 million contract and became eligible Aug. 29 for an extension for up to two years and $136.7 million.

As part of the Warriors' presentation to Curry, the team laid out various paths that included the idea of a slight pay cut from his max, delivering them more salary cap room to build a contender around him in the future, team sources said.

Curry's contract will dip from $62.6 million next season to $55.7 million for the 2027-28 season and a player option for $60.2 million in the 2028-29 season. That will provide the Warriors with around $10 million extra in projected cap space next summer, allowing them to be a bigger player in either free agency or the trade market in the next 12 months.

Currently, Jimmy Butler III ($56.8 million) and Draymond Green ($27.6 million) both have expiring contracts coming off the Warriors' books next summer. Veteran center Kristaps Porzingis has only $3 million of his $20 million salary guaranteed, leaving the Warriors somewhere between $38 million and a projected $55 million in cap space, depending on what they do with Brandin Podziemski's extension eligibility, according to ESPN's Bobby Marks. Podziemski, who has yet to extend, has a $17 million cap hold next summer.

Curry took nearly a month to decide whether he wanted to sign for his full max, accept a slight pay cut or wait to agree to a new deal.

"We're in a very interesting situation," Curry told ESPN earlier this week. "All the different salary cap conditions of whether I sign for a max or less or whatever it is, I want to be on a competitive team. I want to have an opportunity to have some flexibility because we haven't had that in years past, the recent past. ... This team should have flexibility to make necessary moves if things happen. Those are always just the considerations.

"For me, information and patience is key. It's just a very unique situation all the way around based on where we've been the last four years, where I'm at in my career, what our team looks like this year and the absolute desperation to win. Trying to balance all that."

Curry, who said he wanted "no drama" surrounding his contract talks heading into training camp, opted for the pay cut and security three days before the team's first practice, quieting any lingering questions.

NBA free agency has almost reached the end, with several players landing in new homes this offseason.

LeBron James decided to continue his historic career with the Philadelphia 76ers after months of deliberation. The Sixers also traded for Jaylen Brown this summer, turning the franchise into a true contender with two huge moves.

Meanwhile, Giannis Antetokounmpo is headed to South Beach to team up with Bam Adebayo and the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers have been sold for the second time in 10 months.

Sept. 25

What's next for Curry and the Warriors?

Stephen Curry's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings.

The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in a position to have extra spending power next summer.

By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million.

For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. Both players are free agents next summer.

Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski. The former first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks

Grizzlies waive D'Angelo Russell

The Memphis Grizzlies have waived D'Angelo Russell, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

Sources: Status of Mavs big man Lively up in air

Dallas Mavericks center Dereck Lively II has not been cleared for training camp and his status for the start of the regular season has yet to be determined as he continues to recover from right foot surgery, sources told ESPN's Tim MacMahon.

After playing a key role as a rookie in the Mavericks' run to the 2024 NBA Finals, Lively's promising career has been derailed by recurring problems with his right foot, which has been surgically repaired twice in the last 14 months.

Lively is ramping up toward being cleared for basketball activity, sources said, emphasizing that the team is not discouraged by his progress. Dallas begins training camp on Saturday.

articles.headline: Altman: Cavs built for 'sustainable run' despite missing on LeBron
articles.description: Cavs president of basketball operations Koby Altman said he wasn't fazed when LeBron James chose to sign with the Sixers, saying, "We're built for a sustainable run here regardless of one outcome."
articles.body:
INDEPENDENCE, Ohio -- Koby Altman would have loved for LeBron James to return for a third stint with the Cleveland Cavaliers.

When the most popular player in franchise history decided to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers after eight seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers, the Cavaliers' president of basketball operations wasn't fazed.

"We can't be reliant on one outcome. I think we have too much of a good thing going in terms of our infrastructure, our foundation to worry about one outcome," Altman said at a news conference Friday before the Cavaliers begin training camp next week. "I'm not downplaying the enormity and magnitude of the decision. I just think the way we're built as an organization is we have a great foundation and a great sort of ecosystem in terms of talent, coaching staff, our performance staff and we're built for a sustainable run here regardless of one outcome."

James' agent, Rich Paul, said on his podcast in July that the Cavaliers were the only team to meet with James, while the Miami Heat and Golden State Warriors were the other finalists.

Altman has been able to build a contending roster since James' second departure in 2018 after he led the Cavs to four straight trips to the NBA Finals and the franchise's first championship in 2016.

Cleveland has won at least 50 games the past two years and reached the Eastern Conference finals last season for the first time since 2018. The team was swept in four games by the eventual NBA champion New York Knicks.

The Cavs quickly pivoted after James' decision and addressed their need for a wing player, acquiring Peyton Watson in a five-team trade and signing him to a four-year, $88 million contract. On the first day of free agency, Donovan Mitchell signed a four-year, $273 million contract extension.

James Harden, who was acquired near the trade deadline, signed a three-year, $97 million extension that gave the Cavaliers some flexibility under the salary cap by going below both aprons.

"You go through the list and zoom out and say, 'OK, was this offseason a success? Were we able to get better? Did we look at the future? Did we get more financial flexibility, more sustainability with the roster?' All of those things lead me to say this was a really good offseason in spite of that one decision," Altman said.

While the 37-year-old Harden and 30-year-old Mitchell are the team leaders, the 24-year-old Watson gives the Cavs another young player who can mesh with Evan Mobley (25), Jarrett Allen (28) and Jaylon Tyson (23).

Watson started a career-high 40 games last season with the Denver Nuggets and averaged career bests in points (14.6), rebounds (4.9) and assists (2.1).

"What I've been seeing in the gym is the defense, first of all. And then he shot 41% from 3 last year. It's a one-year sample, but there's a lot of room for growth in his offensive game, especially the way we play," coach Kenny Atkinson said.

articles.headline: QB Sam Darnold back Sunday, but Seahawks down two safeties
articles.description: Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold will start Sunday, but the defending Super Bowl champions will be without both starting safeties as Julian Love and Ty Okada have been ruled out.
articles.headlineJa: QBサム・ダーノルドが日曜日に復帰、しかしシーホークスはセーフティ2名を欠く
articles.descriptionJa: シーホークスのクォーターバック、サム・ダーノルドが日曜日に先発出場しますが、前年スーパーボウル王者のチームはジュリアン・ラブとタイ・オカダの両先発セーフティが欠場となりました。
articles.body:
RENTON, Wash. -- Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold will start Sunday against the Washington Commanders, but the defending Super Bowl champions will be without both starting safeties as Julian Love and Ty Okada have been ruled out.

Backup defensive tackle Brandon Pili (concussion/neck) is questionable. No other Seahawks player has a game designation.

Darnold missed most of the first two games with a glute injury he suffered early in the season opener. He was limited Wednesday in his return to practice and was a full participant Thursday and Friday. Coach Mike Macdonald said Friday that Darnold looked "really good" this week.

 

"Sam's going to play, and he's ready to go," Macdonald said. "He's done a great job."

Speaking with reporters Thursday, Darnold said he briefly feared that his season might be over -- and that his career could be impacted long term -- when he was hurt on the fifth play of Seattle's Week 1 win over the New England Patriots. After backup Drew Lock led Seattle to a 31-7 win over the Arizona Cardinals and a 2-0 start last week, Macdonald said Darnold's timetable had "shifted quite drastically" for the better.

Macdonald was asked Friday what he needed to see from Darnold this week.

"Really just to see him confident in the things that he's been doing," Macdonald said. "He's been really positive and says he feels great. He looks great, so we'll rolling. It's a medical miracle he's back."

Rodney Thomas II will make his third straight start for Okada, who remains out with a hamstring injury. Macdonald said AJ Finley will start for Love, who popped up on the injury report as a nonparticipant Thursday when a calf tightened up. Love was again a nonparticipant Friday. Macdonald said he doesn't know how much time Love will miss.

Love has an interception in three straight games dating to Seattle's Super Bowl LX win over New England.

Finley will make his first start since entering the NFL as an undrafted free agent out of Mississippi in 2023. Claimed off waivers from the Los Angeles Chargers in November 2024, Finley missed all of last season after tearing an ACL in the team's annual training camp practice at Lumen Field. After intercepting Darnold during the same event this summer, Finley acknowledged how meaningful it was to him, calling it a "full-circle moment."

"You're really bummed about Julian obviously because he's had such a great start to the season and he's such a great player," Macdonald said. "But when AJ got the pick in training camp, I'm thinking about the journey he's been on over the last year and the way he's really gotten his body back and his movement. He had a great practice today. He's on it. He's sharp as a whip, great communication, ball skills, all those things. So I'm excited for him to have the opportunity."

Okada is still unable to practice.

articles.headline: Eagles' Saquon Barkley to be 'fearless' vs. Bears despite stinger
articles.description: Eagles running back Saquon Barkley plans to play "fearless" Monday night against the Chicago Bears as he eyes a return from a stinger injury.
articles.headlineJa: イーグルスのセイクワン・バークリー、神経損傷を抱えながらもベアーズ戦で「恐れずに」プレーへ
articles.descriptionJa: イーグルスのランニングバック、セイクワン・バークリーは、神経損傷（スティンガー）からの復帰を目指し、月曜夜のシカゴ・ベアーズ戦で「恐れずに」プレーする意向を示しています。
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- Eagles running back Saquon Barkley plans to play "fearless" Monday night against the Chicago Bears as he eyes a return from a stinger injury.

Barkley was tackled for no gain by defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons on the first offensive snap from scrimmage and went indoors after being examined in the medical tent.

He returned briefly in the second half but played just 10 of a possible 72 snaps and finished with four carries for 9 yards.

Barkley returned to the practice field this week after undergoing an MRI on Monday. He was listed as a full participant Friday after being limited Thursday.

"I've had a history of [stingers] before. This is the first bad one I had in a long time," he said. "It's also like a wake-up call to me. I've been super active focusing on my lower body and longevity of my career. I probably wasn't as great as I needed to be with my neck stability and strengthening my neck. So it's putting that within my routine and having that as part of my process and kind of the same way I attack everything from head to toe, do the same thing with my neck.

"It's good to have an MRI knowing it's nothing, hopefully, God willing, where I worry about my career and I can just go out there and play free."

Barkley, 29, returned to the game Sunday with a neck roll and plans to wear a modified version Monday night that allows for greater mobility.

Barkley has rushed for 92 yards on 19 carries through two games this season (4.8 yards per carry). He has not missed a full game due to injury in his two-plus years in Philadelphia.

"I don't think so," Barkley said, when asked if the injury will affect him against Chicago. "That's why I'm rehabbing my ass off, to get it as strong as it needs to be. I feel like I'm in a really good spot. I know they wouldn't let me go out there if I wasn't able to do it.

"I'm going to let the game come, and I'm going to go out there and play fearless, don't worry about."
